recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-13502 unless a separate work group decision changes AuditEvent.agent.who target types.
issue_request: FHIR-13502 was a Published/Persuasive Security WG STU3 change request asking to add PractitionerRole to AuditEvent.agent.reference, with a 3-0-0 vote on 2017-07-11.
initial_application: Commit a274b37aa7315afdba06a5c14005964cc9d8d2ba (GF#13502) added PractitionerRole to the AuditEvent.agent.reference Reference target list in source/auditevent/auditevent-spreadsheet.xml. Commit 6c0a0563b3ac6a188b713f2f1a04ff26229100cf later renamed AuditEvent.agent.reference to AuditEvent.agent.who while preserving PractitionerRole, and commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 carried the target into the current StructureDefinition XML source.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists auditevent=AuditEvent as an active resource, so source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml is current build source. The current AuditEvent.agent.who definition includes targetProfile http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/PractitionerRole. Later FHIR-40293 discusses AuditEvent agent relationship/on-behalf-of modeling but does not supersede or reverse PractitionerRole as an allowed agent target. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-13502 found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current active source already satisfies the issue after the element was renamed from agent.reference to agent.who.

related_jiras.note: Later Security WG issue about representing relationships among multiple AuditEvent agents; it confirms adjacent modeling concerns but does not change the PractitionerRole target allowed by FHIR-13502.
